body:
OBSERVED, confirmed independently (Opus).

Classic requires the CONJUNCTION of both role bits before it will even render the
delete control: `cps/templates/detail.html:1202` —
`delete_book(current_user.role_delete_books() and current_user.role_edit())`.

The SPA requires only one: `frontend/src/pages/BookDetail.tsx:557` —
`me?.role?.delete_books && (...)`. The API agrees with the SPA, not with classic:
`cps/api/edit.py:409-425` checks `current_user.role_delete_books()` alone.

`edit` and `delete_books` are independently assignable bits (`cps/constants.py`),
and the SPA's own admin UI exposes them as separate toggles
(`frontend/src/pages/Admin.tsx:51-60`, mapped at `cps/api/admin.py:37-48`).

So an account provisioned as delete-but-not-edit is denied whole-book deletion in the
classic UI and granted it in the new one. Note the code comment at BookDetail.tsx:554-556
says "The server still re-checks the role" — true, but the server re-checks the WEAKER
condition, so the comment reads as reassurance while describing the gap.

This needs a policy decision before the SPA becomes the only UI: either classic's
conjunction is the intended rule (then fix the API and the SPA), or the single bit is
(then classic is over-restrictive and the intent should be written down). Do not resolve
it by aligning the UI to the current API without deciding which is correct.

resolution.note: Shipped in #2119: whole-book conjunction had landed in d8bdb1cb88; format delete now also requires delete_books AND edit via one _require_book_delete guard; SPA controls share canDeleteBooks. Policy: classic's conjunction is the intended rule.

title: New UI grants whole-book delete to delete-without-edit users; classic requires both roles
